## Simple explanation

A REST API lets software request or modify resources over HTTP using
conventional operations. An AI application might use one to submit
inference requests or retrieve model metadata.

## Technical explanation

REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style based on
constraints such as a uniform interface, stateless communication, and
cacheable responses. In practice, many APIs described as REST use HTTP
methods and resource-oriented URLs, often with JSON representations.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

REST APIs are a common way to integrate model services with applications,
data systems, and deployment platforms. Clear schemas, authentication,
timeouts, rate limits, and error semantics are needed for reliable
production use.

## How it works

A client sends an HTTP request to a resource endpoint with a method such as
GET or POST, headers, and possibly a body. The server validates the request
and returns a status code and representation. Statelessness means the
server does not rely on hidden client session state between requests.

## Practical example

A client might send a POST request with text and model options to an
inference endpoint. The service validates the payload, performs inference,
and returns a structured response with an appropriate status code.

## Common misconceptions

- JSON over HTTP does not by itself make an API RESTful.
- Stateless requests can still depend on databases, authentication, and
  other server-side state.
